in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child. My son Alex is 5 years old, and I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you some questions about your situation:

**Where do you currently live - are you living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. We're based in Leeds.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you!

**Is Alex living with you in your household in Leeds?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

Now I need to understand a bit more about your relationship with Alex:

**Are you Alex's parent, or do you have another relationship to him (for example, are you a guardian, foster carer, or other carer)?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, such as Alex's other parent or another family member?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know, thank you.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you and Alex both normally living in the UK? By this I mean, is the UK your main home where you usually live, rather than being here temporarily?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, the UK is our main home. We live here permanently - this is where we're based and where Alex goes to school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

One final question:

**Are you currently responsible for Alex in terms of providing for his care and upbringing? For example, do you make decisions about his welfare, education, and day-to-day needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm fully responsible for Alex - I take care of all his day-to-day needs, make decisions about his schooling, healthcare, and everything else to do with raising him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

✓ Alex is 5 years old (under 16)
✓ You are his parent and responsible for his care and upbringing
✓ Alex lives with you in your household
✓ You both normally live in the UK (Leeds is your main home)
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You meet all the key eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. You can proceed with making a claim if you haven't already done so. Child Benefit is paid to help with the costs of raising children, and you can claim it for each child you're responsible for.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
